B"H
# Phase 4 — Discovery: Four Vessels, One Movie Language

> The Awtsmoos renews each vessel without making every vessel the same;
> Awtsmoos.com can share one living movie grammar while each studio keeps its name.

## Observed app roles
- `apps/animator`: mature generative animation engine with structured movie plans, characters, performances, sequences, shots, dialogue, objects, titles, effects tracks, custom Canvas/WebGL runtime, WebCodecs export, and extensive verification.
- `apps/nesher-studio`: NLE/recording/export product with clips/tracks/history plus WebCodecs capability negotiation and browser export.
- `apps/video-editor`: deliberately lightweight media timeline whose clip truth is URL/type/start/duration plus captions/playback.
- `apps/mitzvah-studio`: portable `awtsmoos.world.v1` world authoring model with objects carrying shape, position, rotation, scale, material role, color, size, and deterministic seed.
- `apps/slides`: no meaningful movie-engine evidence in current scan; excluded unless a dependency trace later proves otherwise.

## Existing Animator movie grammar
A plan already carries `duration`, `characters`, `sequences`, `shots`, `dialogue`, `performances`, `objects`, `titleCards`, `textBoxes`, assets, and settings. `MoviePlanCompiler` turns that into editable NLE tracks for composition, camera, video, titles, dialogue, audio, action, emotion, gesture, props, effects, and music.

## Existing Nesher grammar
Timeline state carries `fps`, `duration`, playhead, zoom, markers, tracks, history. Clips carry `assetId`, track, start, duration, inPoint, volume, opacity, mute/disabled, and fades. Export planning negotiates actual browser support rather than assuming codecs.

## Existing Mitzvah grammar
`awtsmoos.world.v1` is a portable object document. It is useful as a spatial/world adapter target, not as a substitute for a cinematic timeline.

## Existing lightweight editor grammar
Media/timing is the intentional scope. It should receive a flattened movie representation instead of inheriting an entire renderer stack.

## Architectural conclusion
Create `shared/movie/` as an ES-module interchange and AI-director layer. Preserve Animator as the highest-fidelity cinematic backend, Nesher as NLE/export backend, Mitzvah as spatial/world authoring backend, and Video Editor as fast media-timeline backend. Capability manifests make fidelity explicit.
